subject: cat-act-2011-lqa
note: 5A, 2026-10-01, against the Cat Act 2011 compilation 00-l0-01 and the Cat Regulations 2012 compilation 02-b0-00. Fifteen forks. A fork is not a defect: whether leaving the choice open is one (category U) is for 7A. Every fork but FORK-01's reading C is asserted both ways in cat-cases.l4, on the facts that divide the readings; the assertions of the reading not taken are marked 'reading B' (or 'reading C') there. Reading ids end -A for the reading taken.

entries.question: On which day does a cat 'reach 6 months of age' (and a person cease to be 'a child under 18 years of age')? The Act does not say how age is reckoned, and the Interpretation Act reckons periods of months, not ages.

readings.reading: Age is a period of calendar months beginning on the day of birth (IA s. 62); the age is reached on the day after the period ends: the numerically corresponding day, or the 1st of the next month where there is none. Born 15 Aug 2025: 6 months on 15 Feb 2026; born 31 Aug 2025: on 1 Mar 2026.
The period of age is 'reckoned from' the day of birth, so IA s. 61(1)(b) excludes that day: born 15 Aug 2025, 6 months on 16 Feb 2026.
The common-law rule that a person attains an age at the beginning of the day before the anniversary: born 15 Aug 2025, 6 months on 14 Feb 2026.

entries.why: It matches ordinary usage (a cat born on 15 August is six months old on 15 February) and IA s. 62's own scheme of numerically corresponding dates. Reading B treats a birthday as a day 'from' which time is reckoned, which the Act does not say. Reading C is a rule about persons' legal capacity, not a reckoning the Act adopts; whether it survives in WA was not checked (no source in the 0H or 3H set).
entries.asserted: cat-cases.l4, section 'Part 1 -- age (FORK-01)': readings A and B on a cat born 15 Aug 2025 (14, 15, 16 Feb 2026) and on month-end births (31 Aug 2025, 31 Aug 2027, where the readings agree). Reading C is not encoded.

entries.question: When the person who keeps an unregistered cat is a child, is the child still an owner beside the parent or guardian, or does (c) substitute the parent or guardian for the child?

readings.reading: Cumulative: 'any of these persons' -- the child is an owner under (b) and the parent or guardian is an owner too under (c).
Substitution: where the (b) person is a child, the owner is the parent or guardian instead.

entries.why: The chapeau says the owner 'means any of these persons', and (c) adds a person rather than excluding one. Reading B gives effect to s. 9(2)(a) (a child cannot register) but nothing in s. 4 says the child ceases to be an owner.
entries.asserted: cat-cases.l4, 'Part 1 -- s 4 Owner (FORK-02)': on Mo, kept by Kit (a child), reading A gives owners Kit and Ana, reading B gives Ana alone.

entries.question: 'The cat has been kept by the person for less than 14 days': for an owner who is an owner through someone else's keeping (a parent under s. 4(1)(c), an owner of a business that keeps the cat), how long has 'the person' kept the cat?

readings.reading: The keeping that makes them an owner is attributed to them: they have kept the cat since the child or the business began keeping it.
Only the person's own keeping counts: a parent or business owner who does not personally keep the cat has kept it for no time, so s. 5(2)(a) always disapplies s. 5(1) for them.

entries.why: Reading B would make s. 4(1)(c) and the business-owner limb of s. 4(1)(b) idle for s. 5, the section they most obviously serve. Reading B is the more literal.
entries.asserted: cat-cases.l4, 'Division 1 -- s 5': on Mo (kept by Kit since 1 Mar 2026), reading A puts Ana within s. 5(1) on 20 Mar 2026, reading B keeps her within s. 5(2)(a); the same on Biz and its business owner Ben.

entries.question: How are the days counted in 'has been kept ... for less than 14 days' and 'has been resident ... for less than 14 days'? IA s. 61 speaks of periods reckoned from a day and of days between two events, not of how long a state has lasted.

readings.reading: As a period reckoned from the first day (IA s. 61(1)(b)) or as days between two events (s. 61(1)(g)): the first day is not counted. Kept from 1 Mar: within s. 5(2)(a) through 14 Mar; s. 5(1) bites on 15 Mar.
Both the first day and the current day are counted: kept from 1 Mar, the 14th day is 14 Mar, and s. 5(1) bites then.

entries.why: IA s. 61(1)(b) and (g) both exclude the first day, and nothing in s. 5(2) points to inclusive counting.
entries.asserted: cat-cases.l4, 'Division 1 -- s 5': on Max (kept from 1 Mar 2026), reading A exempt on 14 Mar and not on 15 Mar; reading B not exempt on 14 Mar, exempt on 13 Mar.

entries.question: A one-year registration has effect 'until ... the next 31 October'. For a registration taking effect on 31 October, is that the same day or 31 October a year later?

readings.reading: The first 31 October after the day it takes effect: from 31 Oct 2026, until 31 Oct 2027.
The next 31 October on or after that day: from 31 Oct 2026, until 31 Oct 2026, a registration of one day.

entries.why: 'The next 31 October', said on 31 October, ordinarily means a year away, and reading B makes a one-year registration last a day.
entries.asserted: cat-cases.l4, 'Regulations -- r 12 periods': from 31 Oct 2026, reading A 31 Oct 2027, reading B 31 Oct 2026; from 30 Oct and 1 Nov the readings agree.

entries.provision: Cat Regulations 2012 r. 12(2)(a)(ii); Interpretation Act 1984 ss. 5 ('year'), 62(3)
entries.question: A 3-year registration has effect until '31 October in the final year of that period'. Which 31 October, when the registration does not take effect on 1 November?

readings.reading: The 31 October falling within the last 12 months of the 3-year period beginning on the day it takes effect (IA ss. 5, 62(3)). From 1 Mar 2026: 31 Oct 2028. From 31 Oct 2026: 31 Oct 2028 (the period ends 30 Oct 2029).
31 October of the calendar year in which the 3-year period ends. From 1 Mar 2026: 31 Oct 2029, more than three years.
The one-year rule applied three times: the third 31 October after the day it takes effect. From 1 Mar 2026: 31 Oct 2028; from 31 Oct 2026: 31 Oct 2029.

entries.why: It is the only reading under which the 31 October is 'in' the period at all, as the words require. B reads 'year' as a calendar year, which IA s. 5 does not. C gives the most coherent scheme with r. 12(2)(a)(i) but, for a registration taking effect on 31 October, picks a 31 October outside the period. Reading A's consequence -- two years and a day for a registration taking effect on 31 October -- is recorded in ENCODING-NOTES.md for 7A.
entries.asserted: cat-cases.l4, 'Regulations -- r 12 periods': A and B on 1 Mar 2026 (2028 against 2029) and agreeing on 1 Nov 2026; A and C on 31 Oct 2026 (2028 against 2029) and agreeing on 1 Mar 2026.

entries.question: The $10 one-year fee applies 'if application is for grant of registration and is made after 31 May for registration until the next 31 October'. After which 31 May?

readings.reading: After the 31 May that precedes the 31 October on which the registration will end: applications made from 1 June to 31 October.
After 31 May of the calendar year of the application: applications made from 1 June to 31 December, so a grant in November or December -- registration for 11 or 12 months -- costs $10.

entries.why: The words tie 'after 31 May' to 'registration until the next 31 October': the half-price fee is for a registration of five months or less. Read without that tie, every day of the year is after some 31 May.
entries.asserted: cat-cases.l4, 'Division 1 -- ss 8, 9': an application of 15 Nov 2026 is within reading B and not reading A ($20 under A); 31 May and 1 June 2026 as boundaries.

entries.provision: Cat Regulations 2012 r. 19, with r. 9(1), (3)(b); Cat Act 2011 s. 23(3)
entries.question: Section 23(1) and (2) do not apply to a transfer 'to an organisation or person set out in regulation 9'. Are the SAFE entities 'set out in regulation 9'? r. 9 names them in its definition (r. 9(1)) and as bodies that place cats into foster care (r. 9(3)(b)), not as custodians.

readings.reading: Yes: they are set out in r. 9, so a transfer to a SAFE entity is outside s. 23.
No: r. 19 means the custodians whose custody exempts a cat under r. 9(2)-(3), and the SAFE entities are not among the r. 9(2) custodians.

entries.why: r. 19 says 'set out in regulation 9', not 'in regulation 9(2)', and r. 9 sets the SAFE entities out by name.
entries.asserted: cat-cases.l4, 'Division 4': a gift of Tom to Saving Animals from Euthanasia Incorporated is outside s. 23 on reading A; reading B's r. 19 test returns false for the same recipient.

entries.question: 'The person has been resident in the State for less than 14 days': does it reach a person who is not resident in the State at all?

readings.reading: No: the paragraph presupposes residence. A non-resident whose cat is ordinarily kept in a district is not within s. 5(2)(b).
Yes: a non-resident has been resident for no days, which is less than 14, so s. 5(1) never applies to them.

entries.why: The paragraph is a period of grace for newcomers; reading B turns it into a permanent exemption for every non-resident owner.
entries.asserted: cat-cases.l4, 'Division 1 -- s 5': on Vic (not resident), reading A puts him within s. 5(1) on 1 Oct 2026, reading B within s. 5(2)(b).

entries.question: 'Convicted ... of 2 or more offences against any of the following -- (i) this Act; (ii) the Dog Act 1976; (iii) the Animal Welfare Act 2002': counted together across the three Acts, or 2 or more against any one of them?

readings.reading: Together: one Dog Act and one Animal Welfare Act conviction make two.
Against any one Act: two Dog Act convictions, or two under the Animal Welfare Act, or two under this Act.

entries.why: 'Any of the following' qualifies the offences, not the count; the list names the kinds of offence that count.
entries.asserted: cat-cases.l4, 'Division 1 -- ss 8, 9': Rex, with one Dog Act and one AWA conviction in 2026, is within s. 9(2)(e) on reading A and not on reading B. s. 10(b) uses reading A's count in part-2-div-1-registration.l4.

entries.question: 'Convicted within the previous 3 years': three years before what -- the local government's decision, or the application?

readings.reading: Before the day the local government decides: the section speaks of what the local government must do when it is satisfied.
Before the day the application is made (as Form 1 Part F asks about convictions 'in past 3 years' at the time of applying).

entries.why: s. 9(2) governs the decision, and the present perfect 'has been convicted' is judged when the local government is satisfied.
entries.asserted: cat-cases.l4, 'Division 1 -- ss 8, 9': Sam (Cat Act convictions 10 Jan 2023 and 1 Jun 2025) applies 5 Jan 2026 and is decided 20 Jan 2026: outside (e) on reading A, within it on reading B. The 3-year boundary (9 and 10 Jan 2026) is asserted on reading A.

entries.provision: Interpretation Act 1984 s. 71(2), with ss. 5(1), 14(1), 18(1) (and s. 16)
entries.question: Does s. 71(2) (a separate offence each day after conviction while the failure continues, $50) reach a duty to 'ensure that the cat is registered / microchipped / sterilised', which is a duty to bring about a state of affairs rather than 'to do an act or thing'?

readings.reading: Yes: the duty requires the owner to do the things that bring the state about; failing to is failure to do an act or thing, with no time specified.
No: s. 71(2) speaks of an act or thing 'required or directed to be done'; a duty to ensure a state is not one, and s. 71 adds nothing.

entries.why: The reference register (REF-41) names ss. 5(1), 14(1) and 18(1) as continuing duties for s. 71; the purpose of s. 71(2) is to keep a continuing failure punishable after conviction, which fits these duties.
entries.asserted: cat-cases.l4, 'Interpretation Act 1984 ss 71, 72': under reading A ss. 5(1), 14(1), 18(1) are classed as s. 71(2) duties; reading B is asserted only as the flag 's 71, reading B of FORK-12 -- s 71 reaches the duty to ensure' being false. Thin: the readings do not otherwise change an encoded outcome.

entries.question: 'A certificate ... cannot apply in respect of a cat that is under 6 months of age': is that judged on the day in question, or on the day the certificate is given?

readings.reading: On the day in question: a certificate given while the cat was under 6 months begins to apply when the cat reaches 6 months.
When it is given: a certificate given while the cat was under 6 months never applies, and a fresh one must be given after.

entries.why: The subsection speaks of the certificate applying 'in respect of a cat that is under 6 months', in the present tense, not of a certificate given in respect of one.
entries.asserted: cat-cases.l4, 'Division 2': Chip's certificate of 5 Jun 2026 (aged 5 months) applies from 1 Jul 2026 on reading A and never on reading B; a certificate given at 6 months applies on both.

entries.question: 'Transfer ... includes ... (b) to reclaim from a cat management facility.' In a reclaim, who transfers the cat (the 'seller', who may contravene s. 23 and must notify under s. 24) -- the facility's operator, or the person who reclaims it?

readings.reading: The operator transfers the cat to the person who reclaims it, who is the 'purchaser'.

The person who reclaims: the definition makes 'to reclaim' a kind of transferring, so the reclaimer is the person 'by whom the cat is transferred' -- and there is then no other person 'to whom' it is transferred.

entries.why: s. 33 lets the operator microchip and sterilise a cat 'before the cat is reclaimed or otherwise transferred from that facility', treating the reclaim as a transfer from the facility; and only reading A gives s. 22 both a seller and a purchaser.
entries.asserted: cat-cases.l4, 'Division 4': Ana reclaims Tom, unchipped, from the council pound: on reading A the City of Perth contravenes s. 23, on reading B Ana does.

entries.question: The information prescribed under s. 15 includes 'the age' of the cat (r. 17(m)). Is a cat's growing older 'a change to any of the information prescribed under section 15', so that the owner must notify the company within 7 days?

readings.reading: No: the information prescribed under s. 15 is what the implanter gives at implanting; the cat's age at that time does not change.
Yes: the cat's age is prescribed information and it changes, so a notice is due within 7 days of each change.

entries.why: Reading B imposes a duty that can never be discharged for long (a new change every day, or every birthday), which the words do not compel.
entries.asserted: cat-cases.l4, 'Division 5': on Tess, a change to 'the cat's age' gives no s. 25(b) duty on reading A and one on reading B.
